comment: Gate proposal prompts for the MoE NAS outer loop.
Two variants are selectable with --gate-prompt-key so they can be compared
reference_best : the best gate so far is the baseline and its measured
accuracy is the goal (the original single-reference
pair          : the lower-scoring member of the best (lower, higher)
pair is the baseline and the higher member's accuracy
is the goal. This is the framing the Phase B proposer
SFT trains on (gate_sft_examples), so the proposal and
the training prompt share one format.
The shared interface contract stays in moe_cycle/gate_prompt.py; only the
framing that differs between the variants lives here.

reference_best.goal_with_accuracy: Your task is to write a router gate that increases the mean CV accuracy of the neural networks generated through it to at least {goal_accuracy}{dataset_text}.
reference_best.goal_without_accuracy: Your task is to write a router gate that increases the mean CV accuracy of the neural networks generated through it{dataset_text}.
reference_best.reference_with_accuracy: Use the following reference gate, which achieved a mean CV accuracy of {reference_accuracy} under identical evaluation conditions, as the baseline for architectural inspiration. Improve it by making fundamental changes to the gate design.
reference_best.reference_without_accuracy: Use the following reference gate as the baseline for architectural inspiration. Improve it by making fundamental changes to the gate design.
reference_best.reference_inherit_with_accuracy: The following reference gate is your current router architecture; it achieved a mean CV accuracy of {reference_accuracy} under identical evaluation conditions. Its trained weights are copied into your new code by parameter name. Improve it by extending it.
reference_best.reference_inherit_without_accuracy: The following reference gate is your current router architecture. Its trained weights are copied into your new code by parameter name. Improve it by extending it.
reference_best.closing_new:
Develop your own architecture rather than copying the reference. Your design must go beyond the reference's mechanism, not restate it.

Respond with only the complete Python module between `<gate>` and `</gate>`.
reference_best.closing_inherit:
Keep the reference's module and parameter names for every part you reuse; put all new ideas in new submodules.

Respond with only the complete Python module between `<gate>` and `</gate>`.

pair.goal_with_accuracy: Your task is to write a router gate that increases the mean CV accuracy of the neural networks generated through it to at least {goal_accuracy}{dataset_text}.
pair.goal_without_accuracy: Your task is to write a router gate that increases the mean CV accuracy of the neural networks generated through it{dataset_text}.
pair.reference_with_accuracy: Use the following lower-scoring gate, which achieved a mean CV accuracy of {reference_accuracy} under identical evaluation conditions, as the baseline for architectural inspiration. A different gate from the same search reached {goal_accuracy} under the same conditions, so that level is reachable. Improve on the baseline by making fundamental changes to the gate design.
pair.reference_without_accuracy: Use the following lower-scoring gate as the baseline for architectural inspiration. Improve on the baseline by making fundamental changes to the gate design.
pair.reference_inherit_with_accuracy: The following reference gate is your current router architecture; it achieved a mean CV accuracy of {reference_accuracy} under identical evaluation conditions. Its trained weights are copied into your new code by parameter name. Improve it by extending it.
pair.reference_inherit_without_accuracy: The following reference gate is your current router architecture. Its trained weights are copied into your new code by parameter name. Improve it by extending it.
pair.closing_new:
Develop your own architecture rather than copying the reference. The search already contains a stronger gate; do not restate either the baseline or that design. Your design must go beyond the reference's mechanism.

Respond with only the complete Python module between `<gate>` and `</gate>`.
pair.closing_inherit:
Keep the reference's module and parameter names for every part you reuse; put all new ideas in new submodules.

Respond with only the complete Python module between `<gate>` and `</gate>`.
